newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally to record close on FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally to record close on FOMC.

text.p: Mexican stocks shied away from lodging an intraday record but still held on to sufficient earlier gains on Tuesday to notch up their first record close since February 25.
Dealers and analysts said share prices surged once fears of U.S. interest rate hikes were allayed by the Federal Open Market Committee announcing no changes in U.S. base rates.
"The market reacted well to the FOMC, dealers stepped in to buy across the board," a floor trader said.
Final closing figures put leading IPC share index .MXX up 31.24 points, or 0.80 percent, at a record 3,952.62.
The IPC did reach as high as 3,957.10 points in the minutes immediately following the FOMC decision, just short of a February 25 trading record at 3,960.06.

"We were expecting a livelier reaction, but the outlook has not changed. The idea is that the bourse will continue to rally over the coming days," said Hector Jimenez, an equity analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
The FOMC stated it had decided to leave the federal funds rate unchanged at 5.50 percent and the discount rate at 5.0 percent.

For his part, analyst Roberto Galvan at the Bursametrica consultancy said the IPC hesitated to break resistance at 3,960 points on caution ahead of domestic economic figures expected later in the day.
"Several local data remain to be known which, although the forecasts are good, may have reined in buying," he said.
"Furthermore, I believe some feel that although there was no rates hike this time round, there could well be in July," he added.
Mexican unemployment and trade balance figures were expected after the close of trade on Tuesday.
Financial firms in Mexico City surveyed by Reuters MEX22 forecast a fall in the April unemployment rate and a trade surplus for the same month.

A Reuters survey of Mexico's 28-day cetes rates nN20539678 showed dealers expected the bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to fall by an average of 11 basis points to 18.80 percent at the central bank primary auction, whose results were to be announced Tuesday evening.
Telmex L shares, which accounted for 17 percent of all shares traded, led the advance gaining 16 centavos to 17.34 pesos. The telecomms stocks' ADRs ended up 3/8 to 43-7/8.
Traders noted a hefty cross trade took place in the infrequently dealt Telmex A class or preferred shares, which were up 12 centavos to 17.24 pesos.
The deal was probably part of a buyback, traders added, because Telmex has corporate links with the brokerage which settled the deal.
Overall trading volume .TV.MX was average at 84.2 million shares.
On the broad market, of 113 stocks traded, gainers far outpaced sliders, by 63 to 32.
